# ArcGIS Pro Salah MCP - full reference

> MCP server (FastMCP, stdio) that lets an AI agent drive the Esri ArcGIS stack end to end: ArcPy geoprocessing on .aprx projects and geodatabases (`pro_*`), the OPEN ArcGIS Pro session through a .NET add-in (`live_*`), publishing to ArcGIS Online / Enterprise (`portal_*`), and static ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript 5.0 web apps and dashboards (`webapp_*`). 156 tools in 10 toolsets. Every tool returns `{"ok": true, "data": ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` (usually with a `code`).

Generated by `scripts/build_llms.py` from the code (156 tools: core 45, live 10, egdb 35, geoai 17, unet 14, schema 12, validate 7, authoring 4, portal 9, webapp 3). Re-run it after changing tools.

Key facts for an agent using these tools:

- The server runs under ArcGIS Pro's own Python (`arcgispro-py3`). ArcPy cannot attach to a running ArcGIS Pro, so
  `pro_*` tools work on files on disk. `"CURRENT"` as a project path is resolved to the project open in Pro through
  the live bridge; saves made from the server to that `.aprx` are overwritten when Pro saves, so change the open
  session with `live_*` tools. `live_*` needs ArcGIS Pro running with the SalahAIBridge add-in (0.1.6) listening on
  127.0.0.1:2026; call `live_ping` first.
- Start a session with `pro_context` (project, maps, layer schemas, counts and sample rows in one call).
- Long work - creating a geodatabase, maintenance, replicas, many versions or users - can outlive the MCP client's
  tool timeout (about a minute was observed). Run it with `pro_run_background` and poll `pro_job_status`.
  `pro_server_status` answers at once and reports what the ArcPy thread is busy with. The first ArcPy call after
  the server starts waits for the arcpy import (~25 s; ~47 s measured with a PostgreSQL connection).
- Irreversible or disruptive operations refuse with `code: "confirm_required"` until they are called again with
  `confirm=True`. Ask the user before passing it. `ARCGIS_BRIDGE_READONLY` makes every mutating `live_*` call
  refuse with `code: "readonly"`.
- Never put a password in a tool argument: tools take the NAME of an environment variable (`password_env`,
  `dba_password_env`, ...). Enterprise geodatabase creation and enabling need the user's own ArcGIS Server /
  Enterprise keycodes file: `authorization_file`, or `ARCGIS_EGDB_AUTHORIZATION_FILE` in the server environment.
- Every tool schema is sent with every request (156 tools here). `ARCGIS_SALAH_TOOLSETS` keeps only some
  groups, e.g. `core,egdb` or `core,portal,webapp` (`core` is always kept).
- To turn a workflow into a reusable tool with parameters, use `pro_create_python_toolbox` (.pyt). `pro_create_model`
  writes ModelBuilder models but only linear chains of feature-class tools are verified; it refuses the rest.
- For deep-learning notebooks call `pro_dl_notebook` with only a goal first: it returns the questions to ask the
  user (batch size, epochs, ...) and refuses to write the notebook until they are answered.

## Install and run

```bat
:: install into ArcGIS Pro's interpreter (the only one with ArcPy)
"C:\Program Files\ArcGIS\Pro\bin\Python\envs\arcgispro-py3\python.exe" -m pip install -e .
:: run (normally the MCP client starts it)
"C:\Program Files\ArcGIS\Pro\bin\Python\envs\arcgispro-py3\python.exe" -m arcgis_pro_salah_mcp.server
```

MCP client entry (Claude Desktop `claude_desktop_config.json`; Antigravity takes the same block):

```json
"mcpServers": {
  "arcgis-pro-salah": {
    "command": "C:\\Program Files\\ArcGIS\\Pro\\bin\\Python\\envs\\arcgispro-py3\\python.exe",
    "args": ["-m", "arcgis_pro_salah_mcp.server"],
    "env": {"ARCGIS_SALAH_TOOLSETS": "core,egdb", "ARCGIS_EGDB_AUTHORIZATION_FILE": "C:\\path\\to\\your\\keycodes"}
  }
}
```

After updating the code, fully quit and reopen the MCP client: it keeps the server process it started, and an
editable install only takes effect in a new process. The live bridge needs the SalahAIBridge add-in (0.1.6):
build `SalahAIBridge\SalahAIBridge.csproj`, close ArcGIS Pro, double-click the `.esriAddinX`.

## How the server runs tools

- One dedicated thread imports and runs ArcPy (like ArcGIS Pro's Main CIM Thread). With PostgreSQL geodatabases,
  ArcPy calls made on any other thread failed (`arcpy.ListVersions` ERROR 87395, `ArcSDESQLExecute` ERROR 87413).
- Tools never block the server: ArcPy tools queue on that thread, the others run on worker threads, so status and
  live calls are answered while a long ArcPy call runs. `pro_run_background(tool, arguments)` runs any `pro_*` tool
  as a job; `pro_job_status(job_id)` returns its state and, when finished, the tool's normal result.

## Workflows

### Analyze, publish, visualize
1. `pro_context` on the project or geodatabase, then geoprocessing (`pro_buffer`, `pro_clip`, `pro_pipeline`, ...).
2. `portal_connect` once, then `portal_publish_layer` and `portal_create_webmap`.
3. `webapp_create` or `webapp_create_dashboard`, then `webapp_github_pipeline` to deploy to GitHub Pages.

### Enterprise geodatabase, start to finish
1. Create: `pro_egdb_create` (SQL Server with Windows authentication and `schema_type="DBO_SCHEMA"` needs no
   password; otherwise pass `dba_password_env` / `gdb_admin_password_env`). In a cloud service, run
   `pro_egdb_prepare_cloud_database` (returns Esri's required SQL; `execute=True, confirm=True` runs it) and then
   `pro_egdb_enable`.
2. Connect: `pro_egdb_create_connection` writes the `.sde` file and adds it to the open project's Databases;
   `pro_egdb_describe` shows what is inside.
3. People: `pro_egdb_create_user`, `pro_egdb_create_role`, `pro_egdb_change_privileges` (view = SELECT, edit =
   INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE together), `pro_egdb_table_privileges` (each privilege separately, simple tables only),
   `pro_egdb_manage_principal` (drop user/role, set password).
4. Data: `pro_egdb_prepare_dataset` (register with the geodatabase, Global IDs, editor tracking, attachments),
   `pro_egdb_create_view`.
5. Versioning: `pro_egdb_register_versioned` (traditional through a TRANSACTIONAL connection, branch through a BRANCH
   one), `pro_egdb_create_version`, `pro_egdb_reconcile_post` (check `reconciled` / `posted` in its result),
   `pro_egdb_delete_version`.
6. History: `pro_egdb_enable_archiving`; read the past with `pro_egdb_create_connection(version_type="POINT_IN_TIME",
   date=...)`.
7. Replication: `pro_egdb_create_replica`, `pro_egdb_synchronize`, or disconnected `pro_egdb_export_changes` ->
   `pro_egdb_import_message` -> `pro_egdb_export_acknowledgement`; `pro_egdb_replica_schema` after schema changes.
8. Upkeep: `pro_egdb_connected_users`, `pro_egdb_disconnect_users`, `pro_egdb_accept_connections`,
   `pro_egdb_maintenance`, `pro_egdb_upgrade`, `pro_egdb_version_health`, `pro_egdb_config_keywords`.

### Workflow -> reusable tool
`pro_create_python_toolbox` with `steps` (keyword arguments; `{{param}}` = a tool parameter, `{{stepN}}` = an
earlier output path, `{{memory}}` = an in-memory intermediate deleted when the tool ends) or `execute_code`. It is
added to the open project. The first time Pro loads a `.pyt` it shows a "trust the code source" dialog; until the
user clicks Trust, every `live_*` call times out.

### Deep-learning notebook
`pro_dl_notebook(goal="detect buildings")` returns the recommended `arcgis.learn` model and the questions; ask the
user, then call again with the answers. The `.ipynb` is written to the open project's folder; the user adds it in
Pro (Catalog > Notebooks > Add and Open Notebook) and runs it cell by cell.

## Verified pitfalls (and how the tools handle them)

- `ReconcileVersions` compares version names case-sensitively and silently skips a mismatch while reporting success;
  names are resolved to their stored spelling and the reconcile log decides `reconciled` / `posted`.
- The DEFAULT version is `dbo.DEFAULT` in a DBO-schema SQL Server geodatabase; it is looked up, not assumed.
- Enabling a SQL Server database needs READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT; when other connections block it, the error carries the
  `ALTER DATABASE` statement for a DBA.
- On a point-in-time connection `GetCount` returns today's count while a cursor returns the historical rows; the date
  is read as UTC for non-versioned archives and as server-local time for traditional-versioned ones.
- `UpgradeGDB` fails on a current geodatabase; `pro_egdb_upgrade` reports `up_to_date` instead.
- A SQL Server login that still has sessions cannot be dropped; `pro_egdb_manage_principal` refuses before dropping
  anything and returns the `KILL` statements for a DBA (ArcSDESQLExecute cannot run KILL).
- Esri requires dataset privileges to be managed through ArcGIS, so `pro_egdb_table_privileges` refuses versioned,
  archived and attachment-enabled datasets.
- ModelBuilder models with multi-input tools (Intersect, Union, Merge) or folder/file/layer intermediates did not
  validate; `pro_create_model` refuses them with `code: "unsupported_model"`.
- Registering a notebook in the open project is not possible from outside Pro; the user adds it by hand.

## Configuration (environment variables)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARCGIS_SALAH_TOOLSETS` | all | Comma list of toolsets to keep (`core` always kept) |
| `ARCGIS_EGDB_AUTHORIZATION_FILE` | - | Your own keycodes file for `pro_egdb_create` / `pro_egdb_enable` |
| `ARCGIS_BRIDGE_PORT` | `2026` | Live bridge port (server and add-in) |
| `ARCGIS_BRIDGE_READONLY` | `false` | Refuse every mutating `live_*` command |
| `ARCGIS_PORTAL_URL` | `https://www.arcgis.com` | ArcGIS Online or an Enterprise portal |
| `ARCGIS_PROFILE` / `ARCGIS_USERNAME` | - | Credentials for `portal_connect` |
| `ARCGIS_JS_SDK_VERSION` | `5.0` | Maps SDK for JavaScript version in generated apps |
| `ARCGIS_WEBAPP_OUT` | `webapp-build` | Output folder for generated apps |
| `ARCGIS_SALAH_CACHE_TTL` | `300` | Schema-cache TTL in seconds (`0` disables) |
| `ARCGIS_SALAH_NO_WARMUP` | `0` | Skip the background arcpy import |
| `ARCGIS_SALAH_NO_REEXEC` / `CLI_ANYTHING_ARCGIS_PYTHON` | - | Non-standard ArcGIS Pro Python location |

## Tool reference

Every tool returns `{"ok": true, "data": ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`, usually with a `code` (e.g. `confirm_required`, `readonly`, `missing_secret`, `exception`).
Parameters are listed as `name: type = default`; parameters without a default are required.

### Toolset `core` (45 tools) - everyday ArcPy on .aprx/.gdb files, one-call project context, pipelines, background jobs (always kept)

#### `pro_add_field`
Add an attribute field (TEXT/SHORT/LONG/DOUBLE/DATE).

- `dataset: str`
- `field_name: str`
- `field_type: str = 'TEXT'`

#### `pro_add_layer`
Add a vector or raster dataset to a map (addDataFromPath).

- `aprx_path: str`
- `data_path: str`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_apply_categorized_symbology`
Unique-value symbology: a distinct colour per field value.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `field_name: str`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_apply_graduated_symbology`
Graduated (choropleth) symbology on a numeric field.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `field_name: str`
- `classes: int = 5`
- `color_ramp: str | None = None`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_apply_utility_symbology`
Symbolise a layer by field value using Esri AM/FM utility glyphs. classes: [{"value":10,"label":"Valve","symbol":"valve","color":"valve_black","size":14}] for points; use "width"/"dash" for lines. Call pro_symbols for the symbol and colour names.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `field: str`
- `classes: list[dict]`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_apply_water_utility_symbology`
Apply the classic AM/FM water-utility look to a utility network in ONE call: valves as filled bowties, hydrants red circles-with-nozzles, meters an M in a box, mains thick blue, service laterals thin dashed blue.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `device_layer: str = 'Water Device'`
- `line_layer: str = 'Water Line'`
- `territory_layer: str | None = 'ServiceTerritory'`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_buffer`
Buffer features by a distance, e.g. '100 Meters' (analysis.Buffer).

- `dataset: str`
- `out: str`
- `distance: str`

#### `pro_calculate_field`
Compute a field's values with a Python expression (CalculateField).

- `dataset: str`
- `field: str`
- `expression: str`

#### `pro_clip`
Clip a layer to the boundary of another (analysis.Clip).

- `dataset: str`
- `mask: str`
- `out: str`

#### `pro_context`
START HERE. Everything about a project/workspace in ONE call: maps, layers, schemas, row counts, sample rows and inferred themes. Give an .aprx, a .gdb workspace, or explicit datasets.

- `aprx_path: str | None = None`
- `workspace: str | None = None`
- `datasets: list[str] | None = None`
- `sample_rows: int = 3`
- `max_datasets: int = 25`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_describe_layer`
Detect what a layer is from its fields/geometry; returns a smart item summary, description and tags.

- `dataset: str`
- `layer_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_dissolve`
Merge features, optionally grouped by a field (management.Dissolve).

- `dataset: str`
- `out: str`
- `field: str | None = None`

#### `pro_execute_code`
Escape hatch: run arbitrary ArcPy Python. `arcpy` is pre-imported.

- `code: str`

#### `pro_export_image`
Export a layout to PNG/JPG.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layout_name: str`
- `out_path: str`
- `dpi: int = 150`

#### `pro_export_layer`
Export a layer/feature class to a file (format from extension).

- `dataset: str`
- `out_path: str`

#### `pro_export_map_series`
Export a layout's Map Series / map book to a multi-page PDF.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layout_name: str`
- `out_path: str`

#### `pro_export_pdf`
Export a layout to PDF.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layout_name: str`
- `out_path: str`
- `dpi: int = 300`

#### `pro_extract`
Extract matching features into a new dataset (analysis.Select).

- `dataset: str`
- `where_clause: str`
- `out: str`

#### `pro_field_statistics`
count/sum/mean/median/std/min/max for a numeric field.

- `dataset: str`
- `field_name: str`

#### `pro_find_layers`
Search layers by meaning ("which layer has population data?") without reading every schema.

- `query: str`
- `aprx_path: str | None = None`
- `workspace: str | None = None`
- `limit: int = 10`

#### `pro_get_features`
Return attribute rows from a feature class/table (SearchCursor).

- `dataset: str`
- `fields: list[str] | None = None`
- `limit: int = 10`

#### `pro_get_info`
ArcGIS Pro / ArcPy version, build and license level.

#### `pro_job_status`
Poll a background job by id, or list all jobs when job_id is omitted.

- `job_id: str | None = None`

#### `pro_job_submit`
Start a long pipeline on a worker thread and get a job_id back immediately, so the agent stays responsive.

- `steps: list[dict]`
- `stop_on_error: bool = True`
- `label: str | None = None`

#### `pro_layer_summary`
Feature count, fields, geometry type and CRS for a dataset.

- `dataset: str`

#### `pro_list_layers`
List layers in a map (name, type, CRS, visibility).

- `aprx_path: str`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_merge`
Combine multiple layers of the same geometry type (management.Merge).

- `datasets: list[str]`
- `out: str`

#### `pro_ping`
Check that ArcPy is reachable in the running interpreter.

#### `pro_pipeline`
Run several GP tools in ONE call, chaining outputs. steps: [{"tool":"analysis.Buffer","args":[...],"kwargs":{...}}]. Use {{prev}} or {{step2}} inside args to reference an earlier step's output.

- `steps: list[dict]`
- `stop_on_error: bool = True`

#### `pro_project_info`
Read an .aprx project: maps, layouts, default geodatabase, CRS.

- `aprx_path: str`

#### `pro_remove_layer`
Remove a layer from a map.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_rename_layer`
Rename a layer.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `new_name: str`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_repair_geometry`
Fix invalid geometries in place (management.RepairGeometry).

- `dataset: str`

#### `pro_reproject`
Reproject to a CRS, e.g. 'EPSG:4326' (management.Project).

- `dataset: str`
- `out: str`
- `target_crs: str`

#### `pro_run_background`
Run any pro_* tool as a background job (returns job_id at once) so a long call never hits the client's tool timeout; poll pro_job_status(job_id).

- `tool: str`
- `arguments: dict | None = None`

#### `pro_run_gp`
Run ANY geoprocessing tool by name, e.g. 'analysis.Buffer'.

- `tool: str`
- `args: list[any] | None = None`
- `kwargs: dict | None = None`

#### `pro_save_project`
Save the project, optionally to a new path (saveACopy).

- `aprx_path: str`
- `copy_to: str | None = None`

#### `pro_select_by_expression`
Select features matching a SQL where-clause (SelectLayerByAttribute).

- `layer: str`
- `where_clause: str`

#### `pro_server_status`
Server health: arcpy warm-up, what the arcpy thread is busy with (and for how long), schema-cache hit rate.

#### `pro_set_opacity`
Set layer opacity 0.0-1.0 (converted to ArcPy transparency 0-100).

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `opacity: float`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_set_visibility`
Show or hide a layer.

- `aprx_path: str`
- `layer_name: str`
- `visible: bool`
- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `pro_spatial_join`
Join attributes by spatial intersection (analysis.SpatialJoin).

- `target: str`
- `join: str`
- `out: str`

#### `pro_sql`
Attribute query returning the matching ROWS (pro_select_by_expression only returns a count).

- `dataset: str`
- `where_clause: str`
- `fields: list[str] | None = None`
- `limit: int = 50`
- `order_by: str | None = None`

#### `pro_symbols`
The classic Esri AM/FM utility glyphs available for symbology (valve = filled bowtie, hydrant = circle with nozzles, meter = M in a box), plus the standard water-utility colour names.

- `font: str = 'water'`

#### `pro_toolsets`
Which tool groups exist and which are active. Set ARCGIS_SALAH_TOOLSETS (e.g. "core,portal,webapp") to shrink the ~17.7k-token tool schema sent every request.

### Toolset `live` (10 tools) - the OPEN ArcGIS Pro session through the SalahAIBridge add-in

#### `live_add_database`
Add an existing .sde connection file (or .gdb) to the OPEN ArcGIS Pro project's Databases (Catalog). Needs add-in 0.1.5+.

- `path: str`

#### `live_add_layer`
Add a dataset from disk to the active map of the open Pro session (refused in read-only mode).

- `path: str`

#### `live_add_toolbox`
Add an existing .atbx/.tbx/.pyt (e.g. a model from pro_create_model) to the OPEN ArcGIS Pro project's Toolboxes so it appears in Catalog and the Geoprocessing pane. Needs add-in 0.1.4+.

- `path: str`

#### `live_export_layout`
Export a layout from the open Pro session to a PDF (refused in read-only mode).

- `layout: str`
- `out_path: str`
- `dpi: int = 300`

#### `live_get_request`
Fetch what the user queued from the Salah MCP ribbon (Create Web App prompt / Publish). clear=True consumes it.

- `clear: bool = False`

#### `live_list_layers`
List layers in the active (or named) map of the open Pro session.

- `map_name: str | None = None`

#### `live_ping`
Liveness + context of the OPEN ArcGIS Pro session (project, maps, layouts).

#### `live_query`
Read attribute rows from a layer in the open Pro session.

- `layer: str`
- `where: str | None = None`
- `fields: list[str] | None = None`
- `limit: int = 10`

#### `live_run_gp`
Run a geoprocessing tool LIVE; output is added to the active map. Destructive: pass confirm=True (refused in read-only mode).

- `tool: str`
- `args: list[any] | None = None`
- `kwargs: dict | None = None`
- `confirm: bool = False`

#### `live_zoom_to`
Zoom the active view to a layer (or its current selection).

- `layer: str`
- `selection: bool = False`

### Toolset `egdb` (35 tools) - enterprise geodatabases on SQL Server / PostgreSQL / Oracle: create, connect, users and privileges, versioning, archiving, replication, administration

#### `pro_egdb_accept_connections`
Allow or block new connections (e.g. before an upgrade). Blocking (accept=False) needs confirm=True.

- `admin_connection: str`
- `accept: bool`
- `confirm: bool = False`

#### `pro_egdb_alter_version`
Rename a version or change its description/access, e.g. protect DEFAULT (connect as the gdb admin).

- `connection: str`
- `version: str`
- `new_name: str | None = None`
- `description: str | None = None`
- `access: str | None = None`

#### `pro_egdb_change_privileges`
Grant/revoke privileges on datasets (connect as the data owner): view=SELECT, edit=INSERT+UPDATE+DELETE together; GRANT|REVOKE|AS_IS.

- `datasets: list[str]`
- `user_or_role: str`
- `view: str = 'GRANT'`
- `edit: str | None = None`

#### `pro_egdb_config_keywords`
export | import the geodatabase configuration keywords (storage settings) to/from a text file.

- `connection: str`
- `action: str`
- `file: str`

#### `pro_egdb_connected_users`
List users connected to the geodatabase (connect as the gdb admin).

- `admin_connection: str`

#### `pro_egdb_create`
Create an enterprise geodatabase on self-managed SQL_SERVER / POSTGRESQL / ORACLE (DBA rights). authorization_file = the user's own keycodes (or env ARCGIS_EGDB_AUTHORIZATION_FILE). Passwords as env-var names; OS auth needs no DBA password, SQL Server DBO_SCHEMA no gdb-admin password.

- `database_platform: str`
- `instance: str`
- `database_name: str`
- `authorization_file: str | None = None`
- `dba_user: str | None = None`
- `dba_password_env: str | None = None`
- `gdb_admin_password_env: str | None = None`
- `gdb_admin_name: str = 'sde'`
- `account_authentication: str = 'DATABASE_AUTH'`
- `schema_type: str = 'SDE_SCHEMA'`
- `tablespace: str | None = None`
- `spatial_type: str | None = None`

#### `pro_egdb_create_connection`
Create a .sde connection file and add it to the open Pro project's Databases. version_type TRANSACTIONAL|HISTORICAL|POINT_IN_TIME|BRANCH (+version: a version or historical marker; POINT_IN_TIME needs date 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS': UTC for non-versioned archives, server-local for versioned; count with a cursor, GetCount ignores the moment).

- `out_folder: str`
- `out_name: str`
- `database_platform: str`
- `instance: str`
- `user: str | None = None`
- `password_env: str | None = None`
- `database: str | None = None`
- `account_authentication: str = 'DATABASE_AUTH'`
- `version: str | None = None`
- `version_type: str | None = None`
- `save_credentials: bool = True`
- `date: str | None = None`
- `register_in_project: bool = True`

#### `pro_egdb_create_replica`
Create a replica (CHECK_OUT|ONE_WAY_REPLICA|TWO_WAY_REPLICA|ONE_WAY_CHILD_TO_PARENT_REPLICA). Checks first: versioned data with GlobalIDs; two-way and child-to-parent need an enterprise child.

- `datasets: list[str]`
- `child_workspace: str`
- `replica_name: str`
- `replica_type: str = 'ONE_WAY_REPLICA'`
- `access_type: str = 'FULL'`
- `initial_data_sender: str = 'PARENT_DATA_SENDER'`
- `expand: str = 'USE_DEFAULTS'`
- `reuse_schema: str = 'DO_NOT_REUSE'`
- `get_related: str = 'GET_RELATED'`
- `geometry: str | None = None`
- `archiving: str = 'DO_NOT_USE_ARCHIVING'`

#### `pro_egdb_create_role`
Create a role and grant (or revoke) it to users.

- `admin_connection: str`
- `role: str`
- `users: list[str] | None = None`
- `grant: bool = True`

#### `pro_egdb_create_user`
Create a database user (data owner / editor / viewer), optionally adding it to a role.

- `admin_connection: str`
- `user_name: str`
- `password_env: str | None = None`
- `role: str | None = None`
- `tablespace: str | None = None`
- `os_authenticated: bool = False`

### Toolset `geoai` (17 tools) - deep learning, vision-language and foundation models, interview-first notebook generator

#### `pro_dl_notebook`
Make an arcgis.learn TRAINING notebook for ArcGIS Pro (detect, segment, classify pixels/objects, change detection) to run one cell at a time. Change detection can instead use Esri's ready-made Building Change Detection (no training, needs 10-20 cm before/after images: pass input_raster=before, second_raster=after). CALL FIRST with only `goal`: it replies status=ask_user (recommended model + the questions: batch size, epochs, learning rate...) or status=choose (plain "classification" is ambiguous: pixel / object / detect). ASK the user, never guess, then call again with the answers to get status=created. `options` = model-specific args e.g. {"backbone":"resnet34","pointrend":true}. out_path defaults to the open Pro project's folder. data_path_later=true ONLY if the user said they will type the data path. Add the file in Pro via Catalog > Notebooks > Add and Open Notebook.

- `goal: str = 'detect buildings'`
- `out_path: str | None = None`
- `model: str | None = None`
- `training_data: str | None = None`
- `batch_size: int | None = None`
- `epochs: int | None = None`
- `learning_rate: float | None = None`
- `chip_size: int | None = None`
- `val_split_pct: float | None = None`
- `options: dict | None = None`
- `mixed_precision: bool = False`
- `early_stopping: bool = False`
- `model_name: str | None = None`
- `input_raster: str | None = None`
- `input_features: str | None = None`
- `second_raster: str | None = None`
- `data_path_later: bool = False`
- `overwrite: bool = False`

#### `pro_geoai_check_environment`
What GeoAI is actually available here: Image Analyst licence, arcpy.geoai, torch, CUDA GPU. Call BEFORE any long run.

#### `pro_geoai_classify_objects`
Label EXISTING features from imagery (e.g. classify each building's roof type).

- `in_raster: str`
- `out_features: str`
- `model_definition: str`
- `in_features: str | None = None`
- `class_label_field: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_classify_pixels`
Semantic segmentation: classify every pixel (land cover, roads, damage).

- `in_raster: str`
- `model_definition: str`
- `out_raster: str | None = None`
- `out_features: str | None = None`
- `arguments: dict | None = None`
- `processor_type: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_compute_accuracy`
Score detections against ground truth (mAP / precision / recall).

- `detected_features: str`
- `ground_truth_features: str`
- `out_accuracy_table: str`
- `out_report: str | None = None`
- `min_iou: float = 0.5`

#### `pro_geoai_describe_model`
Read a .dlpk/.emd: the classes it predicts, its chip size and framework.

- `model_definition: str`

#### `pro_geoai_detect_by_text`
VLM open-vocabulary detection: find objects described in PLAIN TEXT ("solar panel", "swimming pool", "flooded road") — no model, no training. Returns labels + confidence scores. SLOW without a GPU (measured 731 s for one 1024x1024 image on CPU) — check pro_geoai_check_environment first, and consider pro_job_submit.

- `in_raster: str`
- `class_name: str`
- `box_threshold: float = 0.3`
- `text_threshold: float = 0.3`
- `tile_size: int = 512`
- `use_gpu: bool | None = None`
- `extent: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_detect_change`
Bi-temporal change detection between two co-registered rasters.

- `from_raster: str`
- `to_raster: str`
- `model_definition: str`
- `out_raster: str`

#### `pro_geoai_detect_objects`
Run a trained detection model (.dlpk/.emd) over imagery. NMS is on by default to drop tile-boundary duplicates.

- `in_raster: str`
- `out_features: str`
- `model_definition: str`
- `arguments: dict | None = None`
- `run_nms: bool = True`
- `processor_type: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_export_training_data`
Cut imagery + labels into training chips. The metadata format is derived from `task`, so it cannot mismatch what you later train.

- `in_raster: str`
- `out_folder: str`
- `in_class_data: str`
- `task: str = 'object_detection'`
- `tile_size: int = 256`
- `class_value_field: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_extract_with_foundation_models`
Run Esri's pretrained foundation models (buildings, roads, trees) end to end — infer AND post-process (regularise footprints, connect centrelines).

- `in_raster: str`
- `out_location: str`
- `out_prefix: str`
- `pretrained_models: list[str] | None = None`
- `area_of_interest: str | None = None`
- `confidence_threshold: float | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_find_similar`
Retrieve everything that LOOKS LIKE your example: label ONE feature, get the rest. No training, no class list.

- `embedding_features: str`
- `query_features: str`
- `out_features: str`
- `threshold: float = 0.8`

- `in_data: str`

- `model_definition: str`

Valid training model_type values by task (object_detection, pixel_classification, ...) with the training format each requires.

- `task: str | None = None`

#### `pro_geoai_text_to_layer`
Imagery + a sentence -> a finished, de-duplicated feature layer in ONE call (detect by text, then non-maximum suppression).

- `in_raster: str`

- `text_threshold: float = 0.3`
- `apply_nms: bool = True`

Labels -> chips -> trained model -> detections, in ONE call. Genuinely long; submit via pro_job_submit to stay responsive.

- `in_raster: str`

- `work_folder: str`

#### `pro_un_trace`

- `out_json: str | None = None`

### Toolset `authoring` (4 tools) - .pyt Python toolboxes and ModelBuilder models

#### `pro_create_model`
Write an editable ModelBuilder model (.atbx) - ONLY linear chains of feature-class tools are verified; multi-input tools (Intersect/Union/Merge) and folder/file/layer intermediates are refused (use pro_create_python_toolbox). steps: [{"tool":"analysis.Buffer","params":{"in_features":"{{roads}}"},"output_param":"out_feature_class","output":"{{result}}"}]. {{param}}=declared parameter, {{stepN}}=step N's output. Adds it to the open project.

- `out_path: str`
- `toolbox_label: str`
- `model_name: str`
- `steps: list[dict]`
- `parameters: list[dict] | None = None`

- `description: str | None = None`
- `allow_unverified: bool = False`
- `register_in_project: bool = True`

#### `pro_create_python_toolbox`
PREFERRED way to turn a workflow into a toolbox tool: writes a working .pyt (handles any tool, multi-input like Intersect, any intermediate) and adds it to the open Pro project. tools: [{"name","label","parameters":[{"name","label","datatype","direction","default"}], "steps":[{"tool":"analysis.Clip","kwargs":{"in_features":"{{param}}","out_feature_class":"{{memory}}"}}] or "execute_code"}]; {{stepN}}=earlier output, {{memory}}=temp. First load shows Pro's 'trust' dialog. See pro_toolbox_datatypes.

- `out_path: str`
- `label: str`
- `tools: list[dict]`
- `alias: str | None = None`
- `description: str | None = None`
- `register_in_project: bool = True`

#### `pro_inspect_model`

- `atbx_path: str`

#### `pro_toolbox_datatypes`
Valid parameter datatypes, parameter types and directions for pro_create_python_toolbox and pro_create_model.

- `item_id: str`

#### `portal_publish_layer`
Publish a local dataset (shp/gpkg/feature class/CSV) as a hosted feature layer. Returns the item id.

- `source: str`
- `title: str`
- `tags: list[str] | None = None`
- `folder: str | None = None`

#### `portal_search_items`
Search the portal for items.

- `query: str`
- `item_type: str | None = None`
- `max_items: int = 20`

#### `portal_set_layer_labeling`
Enable labeling on a hosted feature layer using a field.

- `item_id: str`
- `label_field: str`
- `layer_index: int = 0`

#### `portal_set_layer_symbology`
Apply a renderer (symbology) to a hosted feature layer's drawing info.

- `item_id: str`
- `renderer: dict`
- `layer_index: int = 0`

#### `portal_share_item`
Share a portal item with everyone / the org / specific groups.

- `item_id: str`
- `everyone: bool = False`
- `org: bool = False`
- `groups: list[str] | None = None`

#### `portal_whoami`
Return the signed-in user, org and portal URL.

### Toolset `webapp` (3 tools) - static ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript 5.0 web apps and dashboards, GitHub deploy

#### `webapp_create`
Generate a static ArcGIS Maps SDK for JS app.

Provide either a `webmap_id` (loads a saved Web Map with its symbology &
labeling) or a list of `layer_item_ids` (added as feature layers).
`widgets` may include: legend, layerList, search, basemapGallery, home.

- `title: str`
- `webmap_id: str | None = None`
- `layer_item_ids: list[str] | None = None`
- `out_dir: str | None = None`
- `basemap: str = 'topo-vector'`
- `widgets: list[str] | None = None`

#### `webapp_create_dashboard`
Generate a static Esri-Dashboard-style web app (map + live indicators + attribute list).

Provide either a `webmap_id` (its first feature layer drives the stats) or
`layer_item_ids` (the first is the primary stats layer). Indicators (count &
sums), a category breakdown and a "features in view" list are derived from the
data at runtime and recompute as you zoom/pan. `category_field` / `value_fields`
optionally override the auto-picked fields.

- `title: str`
- `webmap_id: str | None = None`
- `layer_item_ids: list[str] | None = None`
- `out_dir: str | None = None`
- `basemap: str = 'topo-vector'`
- `widgets: list[str] | None = None`
- `category_field: str | None = None`
- `value_fields: list[str] | None = None`

#### `webapp_github_pipeline`
Create a public GitHub repo, push the generated static web app, and (deploy_mode='live') enable GitHub Pages.

- `repo_name: str`
- `token: str`
- `deploy_mode: str = 'upload'`
